cards.text: Genesis has been following Jacob for chapters. Now it turns the spotlight on Esau, Jacob's twin brother (Genesis 25:24-26), and his WHOLE family tree. And the very first line tells us Esau goes by another name.

cards.question: What other name does Genesis give Esau?

cards.text: First up, Esau's wives, from the daughters of Canaan: Adah, Oholibamah, and Basemath, daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son (Genesis 16:15). Grab a pencil, friend, because this family tree is about to get BUSY.

cards.question: Esau's sons with these wives are Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah. Where were they born?

cards.text: Later, Esau rounds up his wives, his sons and daughters, and every person in his household. The man is MOVING, friend, and last time I moved, I didn't pack a thing because an angel did all the heavy lifting.

cards.question: True or false: Esau leaves his livestock and everything he gained in Canaan behind.
Esau moves to a land far away from his ___.
Why can't Esau and Jacob keep living in the same place?

answers.text: They own too much for the land to support
They have another fight over a blessing
God tells Esau to leave the land of Canaan

cards.question: So Esau, also called Edom, settles down with all that stuff. Where?

answers.text: In the area of Mount Seir
In the area of Mount Carmel
In the area of Mount Sinai

cards.question: Genesis starts Esau's account again. This time Esau is called the father of the ___.

cards.text: Then comes the family list: Esau's sons, his grandsons, and the chiefs they become in the land of Edom. One standout: Timna, a concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, gives birth to Amalek. That's a LOT of chiefs. My bakery has one chief, and he's the guy on the gold base talking to you.

Next, the Horites, the sons of Seir who were already living in the land, along with their chiefs. Tucked in there is Anah, who found the hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father Zibeon's donkeys. Out minding donkeys, and he finds HOT SPRINGS. Best day at work anybody ever had.

Then a list of the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites. Eight kings, each one taking over when the last one dies. One of them, Hadad son of Bedad, defeated Midian in the country of Moab.
The chapter wraps up with one more list of Esau's chiefs by their families and regions, eleven names in all. And the last line sums up the whole thing: Esau was the father of the Edomites.

findings.problem: The joke adds a new detail to Papa Dorin's backstory. It says an angel did all the heavy lifting when he moved. In his story, the angel spoke to him and the drawer was gone 'in the blink of an eye.' No angel lifts or carries anything. The last time anyone physically moved him, Mother Miller carried him to the junk drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't share the core action. Esau packs up everything he owns and moves it himself. The joke is about Papa Dorin not packing anything, which is the opposite action. It also mixes his move with his rescue, so it doesn't land as one clear image.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
